evidence_notes: Strong evidence chain: advisory (GHSA-9v5q-2gwq-q9hq) describes the absolute-vs-relative resource wrapper distinction, pre-patch source (Files.java:49-50, 201-202; URIs.java:30-31) confirms missing validation, and PR #7222 / commit ca683170 adds the fix with traversal tests.
Only one representative case (geoserver__geoserver::CVE-2023-51444) supports this boundary. The mechanism is well-defined but cross-case coverage is unverified.
The reviewer's correction from 'request-body authorization mismatch' to 'absolute resource wrapper traversal validation gap' is well-supported by the cited evidence.
main_issue: Mechanism is internally coherent and well-evidenced for the single representative case, but boundary generality across multiple cases is not demonstrated.
mechanism_name: absolute resource wrapper path traversal through missing component validation

evidence_notes: GHSA-h976-6mc8-5w2v confirms missing authorization check in uploadAttachByUrl endpoint.
Pre-patch AttachController.java lines 87-94 shows uploadAttachByUrl without @PreAuthorize; neighboring upload/update/delete have permission annotations.
AttachUploadByUrlVO.java lines 11-13 defines request-controlled url field with only @NotNull.
AttachServiceImpl.java lines 116-140 calls HttpUtil.downloadFileFromUrl(url, ...) confirming server-side outbound fetch sink.
Fix commit 103c79165e3a adds @PreAuthorize("@ss.hasPermission('admin:attach:update')") confirming the repaired guard.
main_issue: The mechanism is tightly scoped and well-evidenced: a single controller endpoint accepts a request-body URL and triggers server-side outbound fetch without the endpoint-level permission guard that neighboring attachment mutations require. The advisory, pre-patch source, service-side sink, and fix commit all align on the same missing guard and repair. The reviewer correctly distinguishes this from path-scoped resource-mismatch authorization patterns.
mechanism_name: missing endpoint authorization for server-side URL fetch
